title: Simon Property Group Fights to Reinvent the Shopping Mall
summary: Simon Property Group is actively reinventing its shopping malls to combat the decline of department stores and the rise of online shopping. The company is investing heavily in renovations, diversifying tenant mixes to include more restaurants, entertainment, and non-traditional retail, and leveraging technology and customer pampering to maintain high sales per square foot and occupancy rates in its A-malls. This strategic overhaul aims to keep Simon at the forefront of the evolving retail landscape despite industry challenges.

title: Former Expedia IT technician pleads guilty to insider trading, stealing information from executives
summary: A former IT technician for Expedia subsidiary Hotwire pleaded guilty to insider trading and stealing sensitive information from executive accounts. Jonathan Ly used this information to profit $331,000 from stock trades related to quarterly earnings reports and company acquisitions. He will pay $81,592 in restitution to Expedia and $380,000 to the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission.

title: Retailers feature high on LGBTQ corporate equality index
summary: Retail and consumer product companies have received high marks in the Human Rights Campaign's Corporate Equality Index for their treatment of LGBTQ workers, with 38 companies receiving perfect scores. This makes the sector the third-highest ranking after law firms and banking and financial services. The report highlights progress in LGBTQ-inclusive policies, despite a year of anti-LGBTQ bills and challenges faced by companies like Target.

title: Netflix Launches Video Previews: How The Company Landed On Its Biggest Redesign Ever
summary: Netflix is rolling out a major UI redesign that replaces static images with auto-playing video previews to enhance user experience and cut down on browsing time. This change, influenced by how Hollywood merchandises content, is based on extensive testing showing that video is more engaging and helps users confidently select content, thereby improving subscriber retention. The update will be progressively rolled out across various platforms, with Netflix continuing to refine the feature based on user interaction.

title: Nokia: A Global Network Operator for the Enterprise?
summary: Nokia is shifting its strategy to focus on vertical markets beyond its traditional telecom business, aiming to become a network operator for enterprises. This move, driven by stagnant mainstream business, could redefine its role and potentially create competition with its existing telco clients. The company plans to leverage its services division to manage networks for large enterprise and public sector organizations, focusing on high-growth adjacencies like private networks and public-safety systems.

title: Juniper CEO On Amazon, Google, Cisco, And The Rise Of The Cloud
summary: Juniper Networks CEO Rami Rahim discusses the company's shift towards software-oriented networking products amidst the rise of cloud computing, competing with tech giants like Amazon and Google, and adapting business models from hardware-centric to subscription-based services. He emphasizes Juniper's challenger mindset in the industry and addresses the impact of cloud providers developing their own networking technologies. Rahim also touches on the company's stance on industry consolidation and the potential impact of the incoming Trump administration on business.

title: Where Millennials Are Actually Buying Their Beauty Products
summary: This article discusses where millennials are purchasing their beauty products, moving away from traditional department stores to a more personal and exploratory shopping experience. It highlights popular beauty retailers like Ulta Beauty and Sephora, along with unexpected and economical options discovered through polling beauty enthusiasts.

title: Why voice will be big and Barry Diller on Netflix, Tesla and Trump
summary: Barry Diller, chairman of IAC/InterActive Corp and Expedia Inc, predicts that voice technology will be the next major disrupter, comparable to the iPhone, and that companies must invest in it to avoid disruption. He also discussed the digital disruption impacting legacy media companies, the success of Netflix, the innovations of Elon Musk with Tesla and SpaceX, and his perspective on the US Presidential Elections and its results, emphasizing the inevitability of tech disruption.

title: IBM Lays Out Plans to Hire 25,000 in U.S. Ahead of Trump Meeting
summary: IBM Chief Executive Officer Ginni Rometty announced plans to hire 25,000 people in the U.S. and invest $1 billion over the next four years. This announcement came on the eve of a meeting between industry leaders, including Rometty, and President-elect Donald Trump, with a focus on job creation. Rometty is part of Trump's advisory panel of business leaders.

title: Amazon Conducts First Commercial Drone Delivery
summary: Amazon successfully completed its first commercial drone delivery in the U.K., transporting a Fire TV and popcorn to a customer near Cambridge in 13 minutes. This marks the liftoff of Amazon's drone delivery program, which is currently undergoing private customer trials. The company released a video detailing the launch and delivery process.

title: Amazon Prime Video is now officially available in Canada — and it's cheaper than Netflix
summary: Amazon Prime Video has officially launched in Canada, offering a more affordable streaming option for Canadians, especially for existing Prime customers. The service is expected to significantly impact the Canadian streaming market, potentially relegating Bell's Crave to the third spot behind Netflix due to its competitive pricing and integrated access. While it offers popular original content, the Canadian library may not be as extensive as the U.S.

title: Costco set to open its first Canadian office, business supplies store
summary: Costco is launching its first Business Centre store in Canada, located in Toronto, in March. This new venture aims to cater to businesses with bulk office and business supplies, directly competing with Staples and Amazon Business. The Canadian expansion follows the success of similar stores in the U.S. and is expected to shake up the retail segment with its focus on e-commerce and next-day delivery.

title: Stuck on Hold? The Worst Offenders Include Apple, Amazon, Airlines
summary: A new study by Fonolo, based on Twitter complaints, identifies the top companies and industries with the worst customer service hold times, with Apple and Amazon appearing as unexpected offenders. The article highlights customer frustration with long hold times and suggests technological solutions like call-backs or queue updates to improve customer satisfaction. It emphasizes that good post-sale service is crucial for customer retention and brand loyalty.

title: Retail’s Best Kept Secret: Pool Distribution
summary: Pool distribution, a modernized logistics strategy, is increasingly vital for store replenishment in the retail sector, offering speed comparable to parcel services at less-than-truckload costs. This method leverages shared distribution networks among retailers to significantly reduce costs, increase delivery frequency, and improve inventory management. It provides benefits such as substantial transportation savings, precision tracking, minimal product losses, optimal inventory control, and reduced store labor, making it an efficient solution for keeping shelves stocked.

title: Amazon India top seller Cloudtail’s revenue rises fourfold to Rs4,600 crore
summary: Cloudtail India, a joint venture between Amazon.com Inc. and Catamaran Ventures, reported a fourfold increase in revenue to Rs4,591.2 crore in the year ended March 2016. Despite incurring heavy expenses, its loss marginally narrowed to Rs30.2 crore. Cloudtail is a primary growth driver for Amazon India, especially in electronics and fashion, leveraging gaps in India's FDI rules for e-commerce.

title: Amazon German Workers to Strike
summary: Amazon.com Inc. (NASDAQ: AMZN) workers in Germany are striking, demanding a tariff agreement binding to the retail trade area. The union ver.di announced a "Christmas strike" lasting until Christmas Eve, impacting Amazon's delivery operations in Rheinberg and Werne. This action follows previous strikes and aims to pressure Amazon into better compensation and labor conditions, with the company likely concerned about similar labor unrest spreading to the United States.

title: Amazon Touts Alexa Device, Overall Holiday Sales
summary: Amazon reported record-breaking holiday sales for its Alexa-powered devices, with sales up over nine times compared to the previous year. The company also shipped over 1 billion items worldwide and saw mobile shopping grow significantly. Despite these impressive figures, Amazon did not release specific sales numbers for many of the achievements.

title: Photoshop is hard to learn. Adobe thinks artificial intelligence can help
summary: Adobe is investing heavily in artificial intelligence with its new Sensei platform to make its powerful editing tools, like Photoshop, more accessible to a wider audience. Sensei aims to act as a virtual assistant, automating rote tasks, suggesting personalized solutions, and guiding first-time users through complex software, ultimately broadening Adobe's user base beyond professionals. This initiative is crucial for Adobe's growth in an era of popular, easy-to-use mobile editing apps, allowing the company to maintain its dominance and potentially increase annual sales.
